p4:main.reviewer: Codex native executor — actual source/content/browser review
p4:main.evidence: All requested subparts, original boundaries, concepts/first line/steps/answer/pitfall checked against current question. Independent answer evidence: The stack uses occupied slots 0..top with empty top=-1, so pushing increments before storing; popping reads before decrementing. Each digit pushes its numeric value. Each binary operator removes its right operand then left operand and pushes the result. The explicit valid postfix and representable arithmetic assumptions make the normal branches sufficient for the exercise. At most 99 characters cannot overflow 100 stack slots.

p8:main.reviewer: Codex native executor — actual source/content/browser review
p8:main.evidence: All requested subparts, original boundaries, concepts/first line/steps/answer/pitfall checked against current question. Independent answer evidence: Push must save old top as the new node successor before changing top. Reversing those two statements sets temp->link=temp, forming a self-loop and losing A/B from stack reachability. Pop must read item and successor before freeing temp; moving free ahead of either read causes use-after-free.

p9:main.reviewer: Codex native executor — actual source/content/browser review
p9:main.evidence: All requested subparts, original boundaries, concepts/first line/steps/answer/pitfall checked against current question. Independent answer evidence: The evaluator interprets each nonoperator character as one operand via ch-'0'. Thus "12 3+" is not tokenized as 12,3,+: it interprets 1 and 2 separately and even the space as an invalid numeric offset. It needs a tokenizer and whitespace handling for multidigit expressions.

p7:main.evidence: evidence/independent-answers.json or independent-delta.json; additional defined C11 cases in evidence/verify_lecture.c and c11-result.txt. The increment/decrement value used as index depends on prefix versus postfix evaluation. Top updates do not make a negative subscript valid; no deterministic normal output can be inferred from UB.
p7:main.conclusion: Normal push ++top selects next vacant index (first index 0); normal pop top-- reads the current valid index then removes it; peek reads without changing top. Changed push top++ with top=-1 writes stack[-1] and only then makes top=0. Changed pop --top with top=0 reads stack[-1] after reducing top to -1. Both changed accesses are out-of-bounds UB.

Pop must read item and successor before freeing temp; moving free ahead of either read causes use-after-free.
p8:main.conclusion: After push: top=N,N->link=A,A->link=B,B->link=NULL. Immediate pop returns N item, restores top=A, and frees N only.

p9:main.conclusion: Stacks bottom->top: 8:[8]; 2:[8,2]; /:[4]; 3:[4,3]; -:[1]. Result 1. op2 is the most recently pushed right operand, op1 the older left operand. Reversing them changes integer 8/2=4 to 2/8=0 and changes subtraction sign.
